svg.text: Net labels with the same name are connected. BCM GPIO numbers, physical pin numbers in circles.
A · I2C bus: mini OLED + RTC
Both share the I2C bus. Enable I2C in raspi-config.
B · Buzzer driver (5 V active buzzer)
Pin HIGH = buzzer on. If BZ1 is a magnetic type,
C · Siren via relay (12 V siren)
Separate 12 V adapter. The relay isolates it from the Pi.
Amp GND also goes to Pi GND. Or use a USB speaker and skip the amp.
Free pins for later: GPIO4, GPIO18 (PWM), GPIO22–25, GPIO12, GPIO16, GPIO19, GPIO20, SPI (GPIO8–11).
GPIO pins are 3.3 V. Never connect 5 V or 12 V to a GPIO pin. The buzzer, siren and amp take power from 5V/12V but are only switched by GPIO.
Relay modules are often active-LOW (IN = LOW turns the relay on). Set alarm.siren_active_high in hub.json to match yours, and test with the siren disconnected first.
UPS HAT (e.g. Waveshare UPS HAT) also sits on I2C (INA219, address 0x42). Its address does not clash with the OLED (0x3C) or RTC (0x68). Use a stacking header so these pins stay reachable.
Modem: USB is simplest. A UART-only modem board can use GPIO14 TXD (pin 8) / GPIO15 RXD (pin 10) at 3.3 V logic, with its OWN 5 V 2 A supply and common GND.
Pump motor and mains wiring are NOT on the hub. They stay on the Pump Node and must be wired by a licensed electrician.
